Irene (support): Hey team, a customer on hosted API is seeing intermittent 502s from the edge for some long chat requests. Happening since ~09:10 UTC, saw ~15% failure on a 1k QPS window. Sample trace ids attached in the ticket.
Jamal (sre): Can you paste a minimal repro and a curl that hits the hosted API with the failing headers?
Irene (support): Repro posted to ticket — short request with X-Trace header and a large X-Meta blob. Quick curl we tried: ```curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'X-Trace: t-123' -H 'X-Meta: <very long base64>' 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' -d '{"prompt":"...","max_tokens":1024}'```
Alex (eng-runtime): Hmm, this sounds like midfront/ingress header handling. Any upstream envoy logs showing 502 reason?
SRE Bot: alert: edge-gateway 502 spike detected for service hostedapi-eu1 (09:08-09:18 UTC).
Jamal (sre): I pulled proxy logs for the times. Envoy shows downstream 413/502 combos where header_processing failed: ```[Envoy][2026-02-15T09:11:22Z] request rejected: header too large, sent local reply 502, x-request-id=t-123```
Alex (eng-runtime): If the midfront is truncating or fragmenting X-Trace/X-Meta it's possible the upstream fanout treats it as malformed and early-closes. Do we have examples where X-Meta > 8k?
Irene (support): Customer's X-Meta blobs are ~12k for their batched inputs. They bucketed to reduce size and still hit the problem.
Maria (support): Customer is asking for workaround now—what can we tell them?
Jamal (sre): Short term: ask customer to reduce X-Meta or remove custom headers; recommend client-side chunking and retry with exponential backoff. Also enable retries on 502 with jitter in their client.
Alex (eng-runtime): Quick mitigation server-side: we can add a header-accept-policy to drop oversized non-essential headers at the edge for that tenant (safe flag). Rolling out as a config toggle to midfront pool now.
Irene (support): Noted, I'll tell the customer to try the client workaround while we flip the flag.
Jamal (sre): For root cause I'm seeing header-parse buffer exhaustion in midfront when certain header combinations arrive (X-Meta + x-forwarded-for + cookie). That causes an early local reply 502 rather than passing upstream. Repro steps I used: curl with three long headers and then concurrent fanout 3x.
Alex (eng-runtime): Patch ready to increase header buffer and normalize header trimming order in midfront; needs a canary deploy to one region. I'll coordinate with eng-platform.
Maria (support): Customer reported degraded latency as well — is that expected while midfront drops headers?
Jamal (sre): Yes, when midfront falls back to local replies you get quick 502s which appear lower latency but higher failure rate. When buffer thrash happens it can also slow down the pipeline.
Irene (support): Customer tried client-side reduce and errors dropped to ~1% within 10m. They're okay with temporary workaround but want a permanent fix.
Alex (eng-runtime): Plan: 1) enable per-tenant header-dropping toggle (immediate), 2) canary header-buffer increase + normalization (next 2 hours), 3) follow-up patch to stream large metadata in request body / compressed header proposal (design doc).
Jamal (sre): I've attached trace ids and envoys for pager duty. Assigning postmortem if this persists after the patch.
Maria (support): Thanks — I'll update the customer and mark as escalated to eng. :thumbsup:
Irene (support): Closing loop: toggled header-drop for tenant id acme-inc, monitoring shows 502s down to baseline. Will keep watch for 30m then transition to canary rollout.
SRE Bot: incident note: mitigation applied by Jamal (sre) — tenant header-drop enabled (runbook step 3).
Alex (eng-runtime): Filing follow-up RFC for header size guidance in public docs.
Jamal (sre): Adding owner: Alex for runtime fix, Jamal for monitoring + postmortem.
Irene (support): Thanks everyone.
